chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and complained to him of destitution (lack of resources). He said to him: 'Marry.' So he married, and sustenance was expanded upon him.

key_terms.فَوُسِّعَ عَلَيْهِ: sustenance was expanded upon him (increase in provision)

ai.seo_question: How does marriage help increase sustenance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) relates how the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) advised a man facing financial constraint to marry, resulting in expanded sustenance (*was-si‘a ‘alayhi*). This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that marriage is not merely a spiritual obligation but a practical mechanism for divine provision, linking marital stability with economic relief. It reflects the broader theological principle that obedience to prophetic advice in matters of personal status directly influences one’s worldly and otherworldly blessings.
